v.why: At very small learning rates the network is undertrained in 243 epochs, so raising it helps a lot (runs 61, 63), unlike at already-high rates.
Very high learning rates make training unstable, so stepping down recovers large accuracy (runs 69, 70, 74, 80).
Pushing an already high learning rate higher causes divergence (run 68 lost 13 to 27 points).
Deeper nets are more fragile at high learning rates, so removing a layer helps there (runs 44, 53).
Smaller batches add gradient noise and more large steps, which worsens instability at high learning rates (runs 32, 36).
Very strong L2 over-regularizes, so relaxing it helps (runs 9, 10).
Increasing an already strong L2 penalty causes underfitting (run 16).
With low learning rates, wider layers learn faster and fit better within the epoch budget (runs 86, 91, 95).
Slow, underfit shallow nets gain capacity and effective learning speed from an added layer (runs 51, 55, 59).
Narrow networks are capacity-limited, so widening gives more gain than when the net is already wide (runs 81, 83, 82).
